mainEntity.name: Is a garage conversion or a room addition better for an adult child moving back home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners typically choose between converting existing space—such as a garage or unused wing—and building a home addition or detached accessory dwelling unit (ADU). A garage conversion uses your home’s current footprint and foundation, which often reduces project timelines, but it removes vehicle parking and storage. An exterior home addition preserves interior garage utility and creates custom square footage, but requires new foundation work, framing, and roofing integration. During initial planning, evaluate your yard setbacks, vehicle parking requirements, and privacy priorities to select the right approach for your property.
